I did NOT open codexv6, codexv7, claude2v5, claude2v7, claude2v8, codexv8 or claude2v9 to audit their rosters. priorInvolvementDisclosure.history: I authored the Claude 2 reviews of v2, v3, v5, v7, v8, v9 and v10.
priorInvolvementDisclosure.myV10AcceptWasWrong: At v10 I returned ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES; Codex returned REJECT on two SHOULD-FIX findings. Having now read the frozen Codex v10 verdict, both findings are real and my ACCEPT was wrong. I record why, because it bears on how much weight my verdict here should carry.
priorInvolvementDisclosure.SARIFV10-S1: I found the same defect — codexv6 and codexv7 omitting the advisories member under an unqualified every-pin rule — and rated it merely advisory (ADV-SPC-V10-01) on the ground that no information was lost. That ground was unsound twice over. First, I established 'no information lost' by opening codexv6 and codexv7 to confirm each has zero advisories, and my v10 dispatch did not permit reading those files; it named only the subject, v9, the frozen Claude v9 REJECT and the frozen Codex v8 REJECT. I went outside my permitted read set and then used what I found to downgrade a finding. Second, Codex's actual argument is one I never addressed: an omitted member cannot distinguish a measured-empty roster from an unmeasured or lost one, so the ledger is not self-sufficient regardless of what the underlying files happen to contain. That is the whole point of the rule. Codex was right and I was not.
priorInvolvementDisclosure.SARIFV10-S2: I checked that the three gaps named in SARIFV8-A1 were addressed — exactly-one, multiple, no-primary — and concluded 'all three gaps closed'. I did not then ask whether the new branches were themselves determinate. They were not: multiplePrimaries was the bare token 'refuses' with no stated object, and noPrimaryWhenProduced's suppression of native emission sat unreconciled against placementRule's unconditional instruction to write related entries. Codex went one level deeper than I did and found a real gap.
priorInvolvementDisclosure.consequence: I have applied the read-set discipline strictly here and have graded this generation's omission on the same standard I used at v8 and v9 rather than on the looser standard I applied to myself at v10.

shouldFix.title: The frozen Claude v10 verdict is absent from the ledger entirely, and its three advisories go with it
detail: This dispatch names two frozen v10 verdicts as inputs: the Codex v10 REJECT at eadd17d7… and the Claude v10 ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES at c8f5673f…. Both reproduce at mode 0444. v11 pins the first and does the full accounting for it — codexv10 records verdict, blockers, shouldFix and advisories exactly, and notFoldedThisSuccessor books SARIFV10-A1 and SARIFV10-A2 individually.

It does nothing at all for the second. I searched the serialized subject: 'claude2v10' occurs zero times, the digest c8f5673f occurs zero times, the string 'Claude v10' occurs zero times, and 'ADV-SPC-V10' occurs zero times. The verdict is not pinned, not named, and not booked.
Three advisories are lost as a result: ADV-SPC-V10-01, ADV-SPC-V10-02 and ADV-SPC-V10-03.

This breaks a practice the chain has held wherever both reviewers of a generation produced verdicts. v8 pinned claude2v7 and codexv7; v9 pinned claude2v8 and codexv8. v10 pinned claude2v9, the only v9 verdict, because Codex produced none. v11 is the first generation to have two verdicts available for its predecessor and pin only one.

v11 also folded content from the unpinned verdict without saying so. honestyRepairsFromV10 credits SARIFV10-S1 for the codexv6/codexv7 advisory rosters; ADV-SPC-V10-01 raised that same defect on the same two records. The repair discharges both, but only one source is acknowledged.

The materially costly loss is ADV-SPC-V10-03. It records that the Codex v8 verdict file changed bytes between generations — f7061826…/16317 bytes to bce8740c…/16802 bytes, at mode 0444 on both observations — with its finding roster unchanged across the change. That observation exists nowhere else: Codex's own v10 review pins the file at bce8740c and treats it as simply frozen, having had no occasion to notice the earlier bytes. Dropping claude2v10 removes the only ledger path by which a freeze-integrity question about this workspace survives into later generations.
shouldFix.notEscalatedToBlocker: Nothing false is asserted. v11 does not claim to have covered the Claude v10 verdict — basedOn.method scopes itself explicitly to 'targeted repairs of Codex SARIFV10-S1/S2' and honestyRepairsFromV10 claims only those two. This is omission rather than misreport, which is the line I drew at CLAUDE-V8-S1 and CLAUDE-V9-B1, and I am holding to it rather than escalating because the finding concerns my own verdict.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Add a claude2v10 pin recording path, sha256 c8f5673f9f9c6a204bd051fd67edb04cd7418f2a70e0f5227fb5ee8eea0e39df, verdict ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, blockers [], shouldFix [], advisories [ADV-SPC-V10-01, ADV-SPC-V10-02, ADV-SPC-V10-03]. Book ADV-SPC-V10-02 and ADV-SPC-V10-03 in notFoldedThisSuccessor and record ADV-SPC-V10-01 as folded alongside SARIFV10-S1. Consider amending pinChainRule's first sentence, which currently reads 'Each successor pins the verdicts it folds' — that wording is what lets a clean ACCEPT with outstanding advisories fall out of the ledger. 'Each successor pins every verdict returned on its predecessor' would close the class.

repairVerification.finding: SARIFV10-S2 — the primary-cardinality failure branches did not determine what is refused or which native writes survive
repairVerification.disposition: REPAIRED — VERIFIED on both operative points
howIChecked: A new hostLocationList.validationBeforePlacement member supplies the validation step Codex asked to precede placement. Its predicate is runtime-expressible and golden-independent: 'Count entries with role primary and a locationUri.'

Codex's first point was that multiplePrimaries was a bare token with no object. multipleQualifyingPrimaries now reads 'Refuse the projection through the existing host-owned required-output-failure path. Do not write a guessed primary.' That names what is refused, routes it through the path that already exists rather than inventing one, and mints no new D9 code or exit number — the constraint Codex attached to the repair.

Codex's second point was the unreconciled conflict between noPrimaryWhenProduced suppressing native emission and placementRule unconditionally writing related entries. zeroQualifyingPrimaries now resolves it explicitly: 'Do not write native locations[0] or relatedLocations. opensip.artifactRefs remains authoritative. The host-owned output path does not fail solely for this absence.' All three clauses were needed — which arrays are suppressed, what stays authoritative, and that suppression is not itself an output failure — and all three are present.

I checked case coverage exhaustively rather than by reading the summary: zero qualifying primaries, exactly one, and two or more each have a determinate stated outcome, and exactlyOne routes to placementRule by name. No input to the predicate is left without a branch.

The repair is surgical. goldenShape is byte-identical between v10 and v11, placementRule is byte-identical, and the only changed paths anywhere under /machineSurface are the four validationBeforePlacement leaves.

A successor should fold the cardinality tokens into validationBeforePlacement or make them cross-reference it, and drop the expected.produced conditioning in favour of the runtime predicate.

summary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Both frozen Codex v10 findings are genuinely repaired and verified against bytes. SARIFV10-S1 is closed: every one of the eight pin records now exposes blockers, shouldFix and advisories, codexv6 and codexv7 carry measured empty arrays corroborated by the dispatch-pinned Claude v10 review's own recorded measurement, and the new codexv10 pin matches its frozen file on all five fields with both its advisories individually booked. SARIFV10-S2 is closed on both operative points by a new validationBeforePlacement block whose predicate is runtime-expressible rather than golden-conditioned: multiple qualifying primaries now refuse through the existing host-owned required-output-failure path with no guessed primary and no new code, and zero qualifying primaries now suppress both native arrays explicitly while leaving opensip.artifactRefs authoritative and not failing the output path. Every branch of the predicate has a determinate outcome, and the repair is surgical — goldenShape and placementRule are byte-identical to v10 and the only /machineSurface changes are the four new leaves. The successor diff puts zero of 27 changed or added paths outside the roster under both readings, all five obligations pass with OBL-2 and OBL-3 discharged for the first time since Codex held them open, and D-096, QUALIFIED, G17 and implementation checks are all clean. What fails is that the frozen Claude v10 ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES at c8f5673f…, a pinned input of this dispatch, appears nowhere in the ledger — zero occurrences of its key, its digest, its name or its identifiers — so ADV-SPC-V10-01, 02 and 03 are neither pinned nor booked, including the only surviving record that a 0444 verdict file changed bytes between generations. I also record that my own v10 ACCEPT was wrong on both Codex findings, and that I reached it partly by reading files my v10 dispatch did not permit.
